title: How do we prove evidence was not changed?
quick: We protect the original with write blocking, copy it bit by bit, compare hash values of the original and copy, and keep notes and custody records of every step.

sections.title: What integrity means
text: Integrity means the evidence is complete and unchanged since collection. You cannot prove it with one trick. Several controls work together, and each covers a different risk.

sections.title: Controls that protect integrity
text: Together these controls give a reader reasons to trust the evidence.
points: Write blocker: stops changes to the original drive
Forensic image: a copy, so the original is touched once
Hash values: show the copy matches the original
Work on copies: the image stays as a master
Chain of custody: shows who held the item
Notes and logs: record each action

sections.title: Verification in practice
text: Calculate a hash of the source when you acquire it and a hash of the image after. Compare them. Store both values in your notes. Later, hash the image again before analysis. If the value is still the same, the image was not altered while stored.
NIST SP 800-86 says to use message digests of the original and copy and compare them.

sections.title: When data must change
text: Some sources cannot stay unchanged, such as a live system or a phone that is on. In these cases you reduce changes, record what you did and explain the effect in your report.

compare.title: Controls and what they address
rows: Changes to the original during connection
Errors or changes in the copy

example: After imaging a drive, the examiner records the source and image SHA-256 values in the case notes. Three weeks later the image is hashed again before analysis. The values match, so the image has not changed in storage.
mistakes: Hashing only the final report and not the evidence image.
Not hashing the image again before analysis.
Connecting the drive without a write blocker, then hashing afterwards.
Not writing the hash value in the notes.
Assuming the image hash shows the original is unchanged if the original was not write blocked.

terms.meaning: Checking that a copy matches its source, usually by hash.
The image kept untouched and used only to make working copies.
A device or setting that allows reads but stops writes to a drive.
Built so that any opening or change is visible.

exam.q: How do you show an image is identical to the original drive?
exam.a: Hash the source and the image with the same algorithm and compare. Equal values show the data matches.

exam.q: Does a hash prove the original was never changed?
exam.a: No. It only shows the copy matches the source at the time of hashing. Write blocking and notes show the source was protected.
